newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: France wants protocol to EMU stability pact - Delors.
newsitem.headline: France wants protocol to EMU stability pact - Delors.

text.p: France is seeking a protocol to complete the EU stability pact which will spell out how EU countries will coordinate economic policy after the launch of the euro, former European Commission president Jacques Delors said in an interview published on Monday.
Delors, who has been advising the new Socialist-led government on Europe, told Belgian daily Le Soir that France was seeking the application of the Maastricht treaty.
"Article 103 of the Maastricht treaty foresees that every year the European Council adopts common policies on economic issues," he said.
"We need to spell out how this will be done in a protocol which will complete the stability pact," he said.

Asked about what the new French government wanted in regards to European monetary union, Delors said: "We are seeking the application of the (Maastricht) treaty, notably the provisions which aim to create an economic pillar alongside the monetary pillar."

The Socialist party, swept to power in a surprise parliamentary election victory earlier this month, said during the campaign it wanted a European economic government alongside the future European Central Bank.
"The French government simply wants to respect the spirit and the letter of the treaty," Delors said.

To answer growing popular demands in Europe for greater emphasis on jobs and social protection, as much weighting must be given to the views of labour ministers as to those of finance ministers, he said.

His comments echoed those made on Sunday night by Luxembourg Finance Minister Jean-Claude Juncker who pledged to use Luxembourg's presidency of the EU which starts next month to look at ways of associating finance and social affairs ministers.
That would allow France to have what it calls an "economic government", Juncker said.
France's new finance minister, Dominique Strauss-Kahn, was due to unveil the government's position on the stability pact at a meeting in Luxembourg of EU finance ministers.
Delors reaffirmed that the stability pact, which limits budget deficits after the launch of the single currency, was essential to ensuring sound economic policies would be maintained after 1999.
"But this stability pact must be completed through the co-ordination of economic policies. It is essential," he said.
